arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Fleming argued the Iowa statute defines one crime without requiring proof of generic burglary.
Saharsky argued adopting a means-elements distinction would disrupt uniform federal law administration.
Fleming cited Taylor and Moncrieffe to support focusing on statutory elements rather than specific facts.
Saharsky contended the Court previously used elements to mean the full statutory definition of the crime.
